questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.R.10

Passage: A community college review found that students with reliable evening transportation were more likely to attend tutoring sessions, library workshops, and study groups after work. The report did not claim that transportation alone caused higher grades. Instead, it concluded that dependable transit expanded students' access to academic support services. The strongest evidence came from attendance records showing that late-afternoon workshop participation increased after the college added a shuttle route to nearby bus stops. What is the passage mainly about?

answer.text: A. How transportation alone caused higher grades
B. How dependable transit can expand access to academic support services
C. Why tutoring should replace college classes
D. Why libraries should stop offering workshops

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.R.10

Passage: The report did not claim that transportation alone caused higher grades. Instead, it concluded that dependable transit expanded students' access to academic support services. Which paraphrase is accurate?

answer.text: A. Transportation alone raised students' grades.
B. The report ignored academic support services.
C. The report claimed transportation had no academic value.
D. Dependable transit was connected to increased access to academic support.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.V.01

Passage: The strongest evidence came from attendance records showing that late-afternoon workshop participation increased after the college added a shuttle route to nearby bus stops. What does relevant mean in this lesson context?

answer.text: A. Directly connected to a claim

feedback.text: Correct. Relevant evidence directly supports the point.

answer.text: B. Emotionally dramatic
C. Longer than other evidence
D. Written in first person

feedback.text: Point of view does not determine relevance.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.R.10

Passage: The strongest evidence came from attendance records showing that late-afternoon workshop participation increased after the college added a shuttle route to nearby bus stops. Which claim does this evidence best support?

answer.text: A. The college should end tutoring sessions.

feedback.text: The evidence supports access to tutoring, not ending it.

answer.text: B. Childcare was the only reason students missed workshops.

feedback.text: The evidence is about transportation and attendance.

answer.text: C. The shuttle route may have improved access to academic workshops.

feedback.text: Correct. The attendance evidence connects the shuttle to workshop participation.

answer.text: D. Printed books are no longer useful.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.C.01

Passage: A community college review found that students with reliable evening transportation were more likely to attend tutoring sessions, library workshops, and study groups after work. Which oral explanation has the clearest organization?

answer.text: A. Transportation is good and students need help and the report said things.
B. The report is about college, so the shuttle is obviously best.
C. Reliable transportation matters because the review found students with evening transit were more likely to attend support services after work.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives claim, evidence, and explanation.

answer.text: D. Students should attend everything because workshops exist.

feedback.text: This does not paraphrase or explain the source accurately.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.R.10

Passage: The review recommended continuing the shuttle program while also studying other barriers, including childcare, course scheduling, and internet access. Which paraphrase is most complete?

answer.text: A. The review advised keeping the shuttle while examining other obstacles such as childcare, schedules, and internet access.

feedback.text: Correct. This preserves all parts of the recommendation.

answer.text: B. The review advised ending the shuttle because other barriers exist.
C. The review said transportation was the only barrier students faced.
D. The review focused only on internet access.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.V.01

Passage: The strongest evidence came from attendance records showing that late-afternoon workshop participation increased after the college added a shuttle route to nearby bus stops. Which phrase best defines evidence?

answer.text: A. A personal preference about a topic
B. A sentence that sounds formal
C. A conclusion with no support
D. Information from a source that supports or clarifies a claim

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.R.10

Passage: The report did not claim that transportation alone caused higher grades. Instead, it concluded that dependable transit expanded students' access to academic support services. Which student statement distorts the passage?

answer.text: A. The report links dependable transit with access to support services.
B. The report proves that transit alone raises grades.
C. The report avoids claiming transportation alone caused higher grades.
D. The report focuses on access to tutoring, workshops, and study groups.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.C.01

Passage: The strongest evidence came from attendance records showing that late-afternoon workshop participation increased after the college added a shuttle route to nearby bus stops. Which sentence would work best in a brief oral explanation?

answer.text: A. The shuttle is pretty much helpful because support is good.
B. I think buses are better than workshops.
C. Attendance records are relevant because they show workshop participation rose after the shuttle route was added.
D. Academic services are everywhere all the time.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.R.10

Passage: A community college review found that students with reliable evening transportation were more likely to attend tutoring sessions, library workshops, and study groups after work. Which detail is most relevant to a claim about transportation and academic support access?

answer.text: A. Students with reliable evening transportation were more likely to attend support services after work.
B. The review was conducted by a community college.

feedback.text: This may give context but does not directly support the claim.

answer.text: C. The word transportation has many syllables.
D. Some students had jobs after work.

feedback.text: This alone does not show access to support.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.V.01

Passage: The review recommended continuing the shuttle program while also studying other barriers, including childcare, course scheduling, and internet access. What does barriers mean in this context?

answer.text: A. Decorations near a bus route
B. Arguments that prove a conclusion
C. Workshop attendance records
D. Obstacles that may limit student access

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.R.10

Passage: The strongest evidence came from attendance records showing that late-afternoon workshop participation increased after the college added a shuttle route to nearby bus stops. Which paraphrase is too vague?

answer.text: A. Attendance at late-afternoon workshops increased after the shuttle route was added.
B. Some stuff happened after the college changed transportation.

feedback.text: Correct. This is too vague to preserve the evidence.

answer.text: C. The records showed more students attended workshops after the shuttle connected to bus stops.
D. Workshop participation rose after the new shuttle route began.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.C.01

Passage: A community college review found that students with reliable evening transportation were more likely to attend tutoring sessions, library workshops, and study groups after work. Which response best uses logical organization?

answer.text: A. Evidence, claim, maybe, shuttle, students, yes.
B. Claim: Transit matters. Evidence: Students with reliable transit attended support services more often. Explanation: This shows access can affect participation.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses claim, evidence, and explanation.

answer.text: C. The report is long, so the shuttle is useful.
D. I would ride the shuttle because workshops are important.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.R.10

Passage: The report did not claim that transportation alone caused higher grades. Instead, it concluded that dependable transit expanded students' access to academic support services. Why is the word alone important?

answer.text: A. It proves transportation had no effect.

feedback.text: The passage does not say transportation had no effect.

answer.text: B. It means tutoring caused lower grades.
C. It limits the claim and prevents an exaggerated paraphrase.

feedback.text: Correct. The word limits the causal claim.

answer.text: D. It shows the report focused only on grades.

feedback.text: The passage focuses on access to support services.

answer.text: A. Students with evening transportation avoided academic support.

answer.text: A. The review supported the shuttle but recognized that other barriers also needed study.

Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.R.10

Passage: The strongest evidence came from attendance records showing that late-afternoon workshop participation increased after the college added a shuttle route to nearby bus stops. Which paraphrase copies too much of the original?

answer.text: A. Workshop attendance rose after the shuttle route began.
B. Records showed more students joined late-day workshops once the shuttle connected to bus stops.
C. The attendance data linked the new shuttle route with greater workshop participation.
D. The strongest evidence came from attendance records showing late-afternoon workshop participation increased after the college added a shuttle route.

feedback.text: Correct. This closely copies original wording and structure.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.C.01

Passage: A community college review found that students with reliable evening transportation were more likely to attend tutoring sessions, library workshops, and study groups after work. Which choice best shows coherent focus in an oral explanation?

answer.text: A. Focus on how reliable transportation affected access to academic support services.

feedback.text: Correct. This matches the passage and keeps the explanation focused.

answer.text: B. Talk about shuttles, then grades, then internet, then personal preference.
C. Focus on whether libraries should buy more printed books.
D. Focus only on whether buses are comfortable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.R.10

Passage: The report did not claim that transportation alone caused higher grades. Instead, it concluded that dependable transit expanded students' access to academic support services. What is the best evidence-based explanation?

answer.text: A. The report says transit caused higher grades without other factors.
B. The report says support services were unrelated to transit.
C. The report connects transit with access to support services, but it avoids claiming transit alone improved grades.

feedback.text: Correct. This preserves both the conclusion and the limitation.

answer.text: D. The report says students should stop using support services.

Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q23

Passage: The strongest evidence came from attendance records showing that late-afternoon workshop participation increased after the college added a shuttle route to nearby bus stops. What does participation mean?

answer.text: A. Refusal to attend

Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.R.10

Passage: The review recommended continuing the shuttle program while also studying other barriers, including childcare, course scheduling, and internet access. Which student paraphrase is misleading?

answer.text: A. The review recommended keeping the shuttle program.
B. The review concluded that no other barriers mattered once the shuttle existed.
C. The review said childcare, scheduling, and internet access should also be studied.
D. The review suggested that transportation was one part of a larger access issue.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG4_U01_L03_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG4.C.01

Passage: The strongest evidence came from attendance records showing that late-afternoon workshop participation increased after the college added a shuttle route to nearby bus stops. Which explanation best combines claim, evidence, and relevance?

answer.text: A. The shuttle likely improved access to support services because attendance records showed workshop participation rose after the route was added.

feedback.text: Correct. This combines claim, evidence, and relevance.

answer.text: B. The shuttle was added near bus stops, and many colleges have buses.
C. Workshop participation is a phrase from the passage.
D. The evidence is relevant because it is evidence.
